messages.subject: Shiny server timeframe?
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I wanted to say that I started using Shiny last week and am blown away by how useful this is! I work on a project that conducts vegetable variety trials throughout the country and I was able to, in a couple hours, build an app that allowed us to easily visualize the trial data. A colleague had been working on a similar task in Drupal for over a year...

My question is, and I apologize for any impertinence, but, is there any ballpark for when a shiny server will be available? Any any idea of the likely pricing? I ask because our project is weighing what the best approach will be for sharing our data with the public, and, if shiny server was going to be available in the next year or so and reasonably priced, we'll probably keep investigating it as a very good tool for sharing our data. I know that software development is never 100% certain, but I was just wondering about a very general ballpark.

Thank you so much for all of your work in creating such a wonderful product!

Jared

On Nov 30, 2012, at 9:10 PM, Glen DePalma <glen.d...@gmail.com> wrote:

> I am able to change the layout depending on the selectInput() function in ui.R using conditionalPanel().   However I would like to run only certain functions on the server.R side dependent on the result from selectInput() on the ui.R side.  Is there a way to do this?
>
> I have a many functions on the server.R side, but I only want to run a select few dependent on the result of selectInput().  Right now all functions from server.R side run on startup, however since some functions take time to complete and are unnecessary dependent on the selectInput() result I do not wish to run these until the value from ui.R  is selected.
>
> In another way, how can I restrict functions on the server.R side from running until it is selected on the ui.R side?
>
> Thanks.
>
> Abbreviated Example:
>
> ui.R
>
>   mainPanel(
>     conditionalPanel(condition="input.Page=='One'",
>       plotOutput("basicPlot",width = "800px", height = "600px")),
>     conditionalPanel(condition="input.Page=='Two'",
>       list(verbatimTextOutput("BootStrap"),plotOutput("basicPlot2",width = "800px", height = "600px"))),
>   )
>
>
> server.R
>
>   output$basicPlot <- reactivePlot(function() {
>      basicPlot(x,y)
>   })
>
>
> #### Only run these if "input.Page=='Two'"
>
>   output$BootStrap <- reactivePrint(function() {
>      bootstrap(x,y)
>   })
>
>   output$basicPlot2 <- reactivePlot(function() {
>      basicPlot(x,y)
>   })
>
>
>
>

> --
>
>
messages.body_snippet:
Hi Glen, just check for those conditions at the beginning of you reactivePlot and reactivePrint functions, and return(NULL) if the appropriate conditions are not met.

Sent from my phone

 sidebarPanel(
  selectInput("Page", "Method",list('One'=1,'Two'=2),selected=1),
)

mainPanel(

conditionalPanel(condition="input.Page==1",
  tabsetPanel(
     tabPanel("Data", plotOutput("basicPlot",width = "800px", height = "600px"),value=1),
     tabPanel("boot", verbatimTextOutput("boot"),value=2),id='panel'
    )),

conditionalPanel(condition="input.Page==2",
     tabsetPanel(
       tabPanel("Data2", plotOutput("basicPlot2",width = "800px", height = "600px"),value=1),
       tabPanel("boot2", verbatimTextOutput("boot2"),value=2),id='panel2'
     ))

)

messages.subject: Re: Observe?
messages.body_plain:
I don't know if observe is going to help you here... would it be possible to show more of your server.R that is having the problem?

But to answer your question:

Reactive functions know when their results become out-of-date, and they notify any other reactive functions that are depending on those now-outdated results. But they don't actually re-execute themselves until the next time they are called. This is because the changes that have occurred might mean that this reactive function's calculations might not even be needed anymore. Shiny assumes that a reactive function in and of itself is not useful; it's only given usefulness when called by another reactive function.

If that was the end of the story, then no reactive function would ever get called; something is needed to kick off the entire chain of events. That's what "observe" does; it tells Shiny: this code needs to actually re-execute when it becomes outdated. Again, this is in contrast to reactive functions which tell Shiny: this code needs to notify its dependencies when it becomes outdated, but don't actually re-execute it until someone calls it. In other words, reactive functions are lazily evaluated while observers are eagerly evaluated.

99.9% of the time you won't need to use observe directly, because reactive outputs use observe under the hood. So when you say this:

output$myPlot <- reactivePlot(function() { plot(get(input$dataset)) })

what's really happening is something like this:

myPlot <- reactive(plotWrapper(function() { plot(get(input$dataset)) }))
observe(function() {
  sendOutputToBrowser("myPlot", myPlot())
})

So the only reason you would need to use observe directly is if you have some reactive code you want to get called that has nothing to do with Shiny outputs.

I need to do a series of blog posts about the reactive programming features of Shiny, I know our current documentation glosses over the subject a little bit.

messages.subject: Re: Deployment on a commercial web hosting service
messages.subject_clean: Deployment on a commercial web hosting service
messages.body_plain:
No, it's not possible to run Shiny on a commercial (shared) web hosting service right now (and extremely unlikely that you could even run R at all). You can however sign up for our Shiny hosting beta program by going to http://rstudio.com/shiny and clicking the registration link near the bottom of the page. We'll come out with our Shiny Server standalone software in the relatively near future and then you could host Shiny on an Amazon EC2 server, or a Virtual Private Server at a commercial web host (but still not shared web hosting which is what all the really inexpensive plans are).

Web deployment for Shiny apps is still evolving, please be patient as we really want to do a great job of it! Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Observe?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Joe,

Thank you for the explanation. I found another solution. It seemed that shiny would get stuck when it tried to build a list with non-existant data and stop trying to update the list, even after the other reactive functions kicked in and the data was available. What I did was just put in some if() statement to stop problematic statements from executing until the data got there, for example:

output$cropstates <- reactiveUI(function() {
  stateselect <- as.list(levels(droplevels(traits[traits$crop==input$crop,"state"])))
  names(stateselect) <-levels(droplevels(traits[traits$crop==input$crop,"state"]))
  selectInput("state", "State:",
            stateselect)

})

output$croptraits <- reactiveUI(function() {
  if (length(levels(droplevels(traits[traits$state==input$state&traits$crop==input$crop,"trait"])))==0) {
    h4("Loading...")
  }
  else {
    if (input$alltraits=="all") {
      traitlabel <- "Sort by Trait:"}
    else if (input$alltraits=="indiv") {
      traitlabel <- "Choose Trait:"}
      traitsselect <- as.list(traits[traits$state==input$state&traits$crop==input$crop,"trait"])
      names(traitsselect) <- traits[traits$state==input$state&traits$crop==input$crop,"traitname"]
      selectInput("trait", traitlabel,
                  traitsselect)
  }
})

In the above example (not very elegant code I know), not all crops in all states have data, and I needed to give output$cropstates time to rebuild the list of available states. Before I put the if() statement into output$croptraits, the function would get hung up with the lack of a list in traitselect. The problem then became that even thought the other reactive functions would ultimately revise, the value of input$state would get stuck and I would have to refresh the webpage to clear it...

Thanks,

Jared

messages.subject: Reactivity and Tabs
messages.body_plain:
I've created a shiny app based off the 06_tabsets example. It's here: https://gist.github.com/4207364

ui.R defines one reactive input variable "n", and three tabs: A, B, and Plot.

server.R defines four reactive output functions:  afunc outputs to tab A, bfunc outputs to tab B, plot outputs to tab Plot, and foo outputs to the ether. All are dependent up on "n".

Questions regarding this app:

1. Why does the foo reactive function ever get called? Couldn't the client somehow notify the server which outputs it actually has? That way foo would never get run.

2. Clicking on the plot tab invokes the plot reactive function. Clicking to another tab and then back to the plot tab re-invokes the plot reactive function. Why? Toggling between tab A and B don't re-invoke their respective reactive functions.

3. You'll notice that there's a sleep call in the afunc reactive call, and it delays the display of every tab when "n" is changed, regardless of which tab is visible. Can the client somehow tell the server which tab is visible so that not all reactive functions dependent on "n" are called?

messages.subject: New App: shiny + d3 + GeneNet/ENA = Reconstruct Gene Regulatory Networks
messages.subject_clean: New App: shiny + d3 + GeneNet/ENA = Reconstruct Gene Regulatory Networks
messages.body_plain:
I created a new application using shiny, d3, and a couple of R packages to infer genetic networks. The application is currently hosted on Glimmer at:
http://glimmer.rstudio.com/qbrc/grn/

I'm using Shiny/Glimmer to handle all web traffic, and ENA to wrap GeneNet to do the actual network inference (more methods could easily be added later). I used D3's Force Layout <https://github.com/mbostock/d3/wiki/Force-Layout> to provide some interactive network visualization -- I don't know that it's really the most practical way to view the data, but it's some fun eye-candy.

I had stumbled through a few un-documented features of Shiny (app-specific `www` directories, JS to handle custom Shiny outputs, fileInput() for uploading data, etc.) -- if you find yourself in the same boat, all my source is available on Github here  <https://github.com/trestletech/shiny-sandbox/tree/master/grn>if anyone's interested.

As the warning in the UI says, I've had a lot of difficulty using the `fileInput()` function to allow users to upload their own data. When running the app locally, it seems that Firefox and Chrome both work. But when running the app remotely (as on Glimmer), I haven't had consistent success with any single browser, so you may be better off uploading your data elsewhere and then pasting the URL in.

Hope you find it (or the code) useful!

Jeff

messages.subject: Placement of CSS rules.
messages.body_plain:
How are others adding rules to either their own css classes and ids or
those that are provided by shiny?

My answer is to override the headerPanel function with something like
this:

customHeaderPanel <- function(title,windowTitle=title){
    tagList(
       tags$head(
          tags$title(windowTitle),
          tags$link(rel="stylesheet", type="text/css",
                  href="app.css")
       ),
       div(class = "span12", style = "padding: 10px 0px;", h1(title))
    )
}

It's almost a verbatim copy of the headerPanel function but with the
added stylesheet link to my app's www/app.css file. I hate that I have
to override headerPanel, though.

I've got it working at:

http://glimmer.rstudio.com/jeffreyhorner/PowerSample/

and source code here:

https://github.com/jeffreyhorner/PowerSample

messages.subject: FooTable Demo - Sortable & Responsive Tables
messages.body_plain:
Hi! I've uploaded a little app that uses a few wrapper functions to display FooTable-styled sortable and responsive tables.

The shiny app: http://glimmer.rstudio.com/szakacs/FooTableDemo
FooTable homepage: http://themergency.com/footable

Source code is attached (as well as FooTable files). Please feel free to use it.

Usage (in brief):
1. Requires whisker, plyr, xtable
2. In global.R: source("FooTable.R")
3. Add FooTags() to the UI
4. In server.R use reactiveFooTable() instead of reactiveTable()
Optional: 5. If needed, add a customized 'FooOpts' attribute to the data frame (check output$view2 in server.R for an example)

Remarks:
- FooTable works with jQuery 1.8.2, that's why the code has to load it
- At the moment FooTable is misplacing the sorting arrows in latest Firefox (Windows). Hopefully this will be fixed.
- This is not a complete implementation, e.g. sorting dates is not possible ATM.
- It would be nice to get standardized these kinds of extensions to shiny. I would happily refactor the code based on an example extension.

Have fun!

Laszlo
@cocinerox

messages.subject: Re: Evaluate Query Results As Input
messages.body_plain:
In ui.r, you can use uiOutput(), and give it something you construct in server.r.

I've made an example at https://gist.github.com/4211337, and you can see it in action here:
http://glimmer.rstudio.com/winston/dynamic_ui/

Here's the code:

ui.r:
========

# Define UI for miles per gallon application

shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  headerPanel(""),

  sidebarPanel(
    uiOutput("choose_dataset"),

    uiOutput("choose_columns")

  ),

  mainPanel(
    tableOutput("data_table")

  )

))

server.r
=======

# Some pre-computed stuff in R. In this example, just assign values to a var

data_sets <- c("mtcars", "morley", "rock")

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  # Drop-down selection box for which data set

  output$choose_dataset <- reactiveUI(function() {

    selectInput("dataset", "Data set", as.list(data_sets))

  })

  # Check boxes

  output$choose_columns <- reactiveUI(function() {

    # Get the data set with the appropriate name

    dat <- get(input$dataset)

    colnames <- names(dat)

    # Create the checkboxes and select them all by default

    checkboxGroupInput("columns", "Choose columns",

                        choices  = colnames,

                        selected = colnames)

  })

  # Output the data

  output$data_table <- reactiveTable(function() {

        # Get the data set

        dat <- get(input$dataset)

        # Keep the selected columns

        dat <- dat[, input$columns, drop = FALSE]

        # Return first 20 rows

        head(dat, 20)

  })

})

-Winston

messages.subject: Re: rgl/webgl & shiny for interactive 3d plots
messages.body_plain:
Shiny has an htmlOutput widget that can be inserted into your Shiny app and receive arbitrary HTML. In theory you could take the webgl HTML that is outputted by rgl, and assign it in a reactive function to the output HTML:

output$webglPlot <- reactive(function() {
  // webgl generating code here, return an HTML string
})

Some things you'll have to deal with:
By default, rgl's webgl mode outputs an entire HTML page including head and body tags, which is not quite what you want. You'll have to provide a template argument to writeWebGL, the path of a file whose entire contents are below.
writeWebGL writes its output to a file, not a string, so you'll have to create a temp file and read in the contents. Don't forget to delete the temp file before leaving the function.
writeWebGL takes a prefix for disambiguating different scenes on the same page. You might want to generate a random prefix for each scene that you generate.

Even with all this I'm not sure if it will work, but it sure seems worth a shot. There's no inherent reason why WebGL shouldn't work with Shiny, so I'm sure that if nothing else some tweaking to rgl would make it possible. If you figure out how to get it going it would be amazing to have a reactiveWebGL function that wraps up the call to writeWebGL for you--we can help you with that if you need.

template.html:

%WebGL%
<script>setTimeout(function() { webGLStart(); }, 100);</script>

messages.subject: Re: Reactivity and Tabs
messages.body_plain:
Great questions!

> 1. Why does the foo reactive function ever get called? Couldn't the client somehow notify the server which outputs it actually has? That way foo would never get run.

Yeah, it would certainly be possible to implement that.

> 2. Clicking on the plot tab invokes the plot reactive function. Clicking to another tab and then back to the plot tab re-invokes the plot reactive function. Why? Toggling between tab A and B don't re-invoke their respective reactive functions.

This is because one of the implicit reactive dependencies for reactivePlot is the size of the plotOutput's <div> on the page (unless you pass an explicit width/height to reactivePlot), and when you hide the tab the size goes to 0x0. If you set options(shiny.trace=TRUE) before running the app and watch the console as you switch tabs, you'll see this traffic going back and forth.

I made it work that way so that plots wouldn't render at all if their tabs are never shown. But you're the second person to bring up the re-invoking of the plot when none of the inputs have changed, so we might need to think harder about how to deal with this.

> 3. You'll notice that there's a sleep call in the afunc reactive call, and it delays the display of every tab when "n" is changed, regardless of which tab is visible. Can the client somehow tell the server which tab is visible so that not all reactive functions dependent on "n" are called?

Not automatically, but tabsetPanel can take an inputId which makes input$inputId reflect the currently selected tab, so your reactive functions could explicitly test if their tabs are visible and return NULL if not.

messages.subject: Several App Design Questions
messages.body_plain:
I am trying to create an app in shiny and I assume what I would like to do is possible but can't seem to find any good examples indicating what I might need to pull it off. The shiny app I would like to create has the following structure:
User selects a value from dropdown list (numbers)
Selected value is passed back to server.R and used as input to a function to pull data from a database
Value is used to define/calculate a date range so this doesn't have to be hardcoded and take more time than needed
The end result of this code is a variable assigned to a list of unique values (work orders) from a certain column in this returned dataframe
This list of unique work orders is then displayed to the user in another drop down menu where they can select the work order they want to show data for
This list is then made available to the user to select one of the work orders of interest
The selected work order is then used to subset the returned dataframe
Graphs for that work order are then displayed accordingly
I have a few questions/issues I have run into:
How do I reference the first input variable chosen by the user in the server side code
eg. if in ui.R contains selectInput("choose_ndaysback", "Days Back", choices = c("30", "60", "90")) ...how would I take the chosen value and assign that to a variable to be used in another variable definition
eg. I have tried:
ndaysback = get(input$choose_ndaysback)
endDate = as.POSIXct(format(Sys.time(),"%Y-%m-%d"))
startDate = as.POSIXct(format(endDate - ndaysback*24*60*60,"%Y-%m-%d"))
How do I hold up the processing of the server.R code that pulls data back from the database until after the user selects the first value?
I have tried using using the submitButton("Update View") in the ui.R file with no luck
For the second drop down list...does this field need to be displayed up front (even if it is empty and dependent on user interaction i the first menu)?
I can't calculate the values of the second drop down menu until after the user selects the first value and the subsequent code is executed
How does this list then get transmitted back to the interface after it is calculated?
The code I have so far is below. It's not complete...but i am having trouble getting past the part where the second list of items is populated (work orders). Any advice/help is appreciated.
server.R
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

output$choose_wo <- reactiveUI(function() {
# variable defined from first ui.R input
ndaysback <- get(input$choose_ndaysback)

# define start & end dates
endDate <- as.POSIXct(format(Sys.time(),"%Y-%m-%d"))

messages.subject: Re: Reactivity and Tabs
messages.body_plain:
On Wed, Dec 5, 2012 at 11:02 AM, Joe Cheng <j...@joecheng.com> wrote:

> Great questions!
>
> > 1. Why does the foo reactive function ever get called? Couldn't the client somehow notify the server which outputs it actually has? That way foo would never get run.
>
> Yeah, it would certainly be possible to implement that.
>
> > 2. Clicking on the plot tab invokes the plot reactive function. Clicking to another tab and then back to the plot tab re-invokes the plot reactive function. Why? Toggling between tab A and B don't re-invoke their respective reactive functions.
>
> This is because one of the implicit reactive dependencies for reactivePlot is the size of the plotOutput's <div> on the page (unless you pass an explicit width/height to reactivePlot), and when you hide the tab the size goes to 0x0. If you set options(shiny.trace=TRUE) before running the app and watch the console as you switch tabs, you'll see this traffic going back and forth.
>
> I made it work that way so that plots wouldn't render at all if their tabs are never shown. But you're the second person to bring up the re-invoking of the plot when none of the inputs have changed, so we might need to think harder about how to deal with this.
>
> > 3. You'll notice that there's a sleep call in the afunc reactive call, and it delays the display of every tab when "n" is changed, regardless of which tab is visible. Can the client somehow tell the server which tab is visible so that not all reactive functions dependent on "n" are called?
>
> Not automatically, but tabsetPanel can take an inputId which makes input$inputId reflect the currently selected tab, so your reactive functions could explicitly test if their tabs are visible and return NULL if not.

Okay, I've updated simpleTab to use the id, and I don't think this is the right approach. It may be my slow laptop but I don't think users will be happy staring at a greyed out tab that contains "NULL"  while waiting for the tab to "reactivate":

runGist('4221630')

I understand why it occurs; you've made the tabsetPanel id a reactive input upon which my output functions depend. Therefore they must be updated. However, there's got to be a better way to implement this in the javascript code on the client side.

 One approach is to use "differentiated reactive programming", as defined by the wikipedia article on "reactive programming", and set a higher priority on   propagating data changes to the "visible" tab first, then trickle in the changes from the non-visible tabs.

Or, you could just *not* send data to the non-visible tables until they're visible. This would definitely help the plot issue as well.

I'm going to peek underneath the shiny hood tomorrow and investigate.

>
> --
>
>

yes, it works but the R session is locked during a long process, so the different shiny users are waiting each other process to finish.
I just saw the "fork" of the parent R session as a convenient way to handle this issue...

I just think this issue could be treated more generally with a fork.

Hi Germán,

I'm glad you enjoy the app.

Regarding the d3 integration, first, I'd recommend taking a look at http://rstudio.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#building-outputs . They have a pretty good introduction to what it would take to get a custom widget in Shiny to work.

I apologize for the sloppiness of the code (my first stab at this and I should really go back and clean things up now that I have a better understanding of how to put JS code into Shiny), but the relevant portion is here: https://github.com/trestletech/shiny-sandbox/blob/master/grn/graph.js

Basically, the JS function defined in that file's `renderValue` field dictate what my app will do with the incoming JSON data returned by the Shiny server. In this case, I'm going to build a d3-based object out of it and show in an SVG element.

Hope that helps!
Jeff

messages.subject: Re: passing an object to shiny.
messages.body_plain:
Just put it in a "global" variable--this can either be in the global environment, or, if you're writing a package, in a package-scoped environment.

If you go the global environment route and don't want the variable to show up for the user, you can name the variable with a leading "." and it won't show up to ls(). And your wrapper function can also rm() the variable when the Shiny app is done executing.

messages.subject: Re: widget request: bottons other than "submit" button
messages.subject_clean: widget request: bottons other than "submit" button
messages.body_plain:
The pain you're experiencing here is the impedance mismatch between the functional-reactive style that Shiny is designed for, and the imperative style ("on click, do this action") that most other GUI frameworks use (certainly most of the ones written before the last 18 months). I believe the functional-reactive style leads to much simpler and concise code, and far fewer errors for 90% of cases, but when you start wanting to do things that are by nature imperative (such as saving to the database) then it starts to get... interesting.

I have some ideas about how to allow you to move between one style and the other, but would like to spend a while longer watching what people are trying to do before implementing anything. In this case it seems like your problems could be solved by having a way to access reactive functions/values without actually taking a dependency on them (so that the code doesn't re-execute). Something like:

observe(function() {
  input$add  # take a dependency on the action button
  nonreactive({
    # Some logic
    saveToDatabase(input$foo, input$bar, input$baz)
    # Some more logic
  })
  # Or another way
  saveToDatabase2(nonreactive(input$foo))
})

So this observer would execute when input$add is clicked, but not when input$foo, $bar, and $baz change. "nonreactive" is a terrible name, but hopefully you get the idea.

Any thoughts?

messages.subject_clean: widget request: bottons other than "submit" button
messages.body_plain:
I am not sure that it is fully related to this discussion thread, but another issue I often experiment is related to multiple input reactives : I want to let the reactive operate, only if two or more input are updated.
As far as I understand the current model, it is designed to update one output when _any_ of its input are updated.
For now, we can turn-around that using some "if ((input$...) == no.value) return(NULL)" at the beginning of the reactive function.

I wonder if a signature "update=function(input.new <http://input.new>, input.old)" for the reactive function should allow to include an explicit control over reactive/nonreactive behavior...
(by default, this function is something like "any(input.new <http://input.new> != input.last)")
Anyway, I have no idea if it is feasible :) And also it complicates a bit the current model which is fairly simple and efficient...

Le samedi 8 décembre 2012 01:47:34 UTC+1, Joe Cheng [RStudio] a écrit :
> The pain you're experiencing here is the impedance mismatch between the functional-reactive style that Shiny is designed for, and the imperative style ("on click, do this action") that most other GUI frameworks use (certainly most of the ones written before the last 18 months). I believe the functional-reactive style leads to much simpler and concise code, and far fewer errors for 90% of cases, but when you start wanting to do things that are by nature imperative (such as saving to the database) then it starts to get... interesting.
>
> I have some ideas about how to allow you to move between one style and the other, but would like to spend a while longer watching what people are trying to do before implementing anything. In this case it seems like your problems could be solved by having a way to access reactive functions/values without actually taking a dependency on them (so that the code doesn't re-execute). Something like:
>
> observe(function() {
>   input$add  # take a dependency on the action button
>   nonreactive({
>     # Some logic
>     saveToDatabase(input$foo, input$bar, input$baz)
>     # Some more logic
>   })
>   # Or another way
>   saveToDatabase2(nonreactive(input$foo))
> })
>
> So this observer would execute when input$add is clicked, but not when input$foo, $bar, and $baz change. "nonreactive" is a terrible name, but hopefully you get the idea.
>
> Any thoughts?
>
>
> On Fri, Dec 7, 2012 at 4:27 PM, Thomas Bristow <darcyspe...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > I managed to fix my own problem (seems like it), using a global variable as a second counter and some logic. That way the action button will only fire the dependent function once per click - even if other reactive inputs to the function change.
> >
> >
> > UI_____________________
> >
> > sidebarPanel(
> >     selectInput("...", "...",
> >                 choices = c()),
> >
> >     uiOutput("radio"),
> >
> >     actionButton("add", "add a mineral")
> >     ),
> >
> > server______________________#partial example
> >
> > output$caption <- reactiveText(function(){
> >   if (input$add==0) {
> >    count<<- 0
> > }
> >   count <<- count
> >   if (input$add==0 || count == input$add)
> >     {
> >     return(NULL)}
> >    count<<- count+1
> > return (c(input$min,count))
> >
> > --
> >
> >
>

Thanks, Andrew. Re: the missing column: it is hidden when the width of the table view is below 1024 ("tablet") and can be displayed by clicking on the + signs. This "'responsive" behavior is configured by these lines:

FooTable.R: tags$script("footable.options.breakpoints = {phone: 800, tablet: 1024};",type="text/javascript")
server.R: opts[[1]]$data_class <- "expand"
and: opts[[4]]$data_hide <- "phone,tablet"

If you omit the data_class and data_hide options, every column will be always displayed.

Please check the FooTable homepage for more details.

Hope that helps, Laszlo

messages.subject: Re: Reactivity and Tabs
messages.body_plain:
Differentiated reactive programming is a very interesting idea. I would love to know if we could implement it practically.

1) Low-priority tasks would likely need to be interruptible as new higher-priority tasks are scheduled. I'm not sure how to interrupt running code in a "catchable" way with R, anyone have any ideas?

2) Reactive functions can have acyclic or even cyclic dependencies, in the general case it's not possible to assume that just because the reactive function that's assigned to an output has run and is now up-to-date, that the output is now ready to send to the user. You can see here[0] that we use a while loop to ensure that ALL reactives are up-to-date (length(.pendingInvalidate) == 0), and we don't send any output until we reach that state.

3) We would need to find a syntax/model that is accessible to R users, or at least, not make the current semantics any more difficult to learn or express.

I'm not trying to discourage you (or anyone else) from exploring this or other concepts, just pointing out some of the obstacles that would need to be overcome. The current reactive system is extremely simplistic (a good trait for a v0.1 of anything novel, in my opinion!) and we're definitely open to suggestions about how to make it fit better with real-world workflows.

In the meantime we have the manual workaround for "you could just *not* send data to the non-visible tables until they're visible" and I've been thinking about how we can make a targeted fix for #2 in your original post (I don't think it will be too hard).

[0] https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/blob/master/R/react.R#L96

On Wednesday, December 5, 2012 8:06:47 PM UTC-8, Jeffrey Horner wrote:
> On Wed, Dec 5, 2012 at 11:02 AM, Joe Cheng <j...@joecheng.com> wrote:
> > Great questions!
> >
> > > 1. Why does the foo reactive function ever get called? Couldn't the client somehow notify the server which outputs it actually has? That way foo would never get run.
> >
> > Yeah, it would certainly be possible to implement that.
> >
> > > 2. Clicking on the plot tab invokes the plot reactive function. Clicking to another tab and then back to the plot tab re-invokes the plot reactive function. Why? Toggling between tab A and B don't re-invoke their respective reactive functions.
> >
> > This is because one of the implicit reactive dependencies for reactivePlot is the size of the plotOutput's <div> on the page (unless you pass an explicit width/height to reactivePlot), and when you hide the tab the size goes to 0x0. If you set options(shiny.trace=TRUE) before running the app and watch the console as you switch tabs, you'll see this traffic going back and forth.
> >
> > I made it work that way so that plots wouldn't render at all if their tabs are never shown. But you're the second person to bring up the re-invoking of the plot when none of the inputs have changed, so we might need to think harder about how to deal with this.
> >
> > > 3. You'll notice that there's a sleep call in the afunc reactive call, and it delays the display of every tab when "n" is changed, regardless of which tab is visible. Can the client somehow tell the server which tab is visible so that not all reactive functions dependent on "n" are called?
> >
> > Not automatically, but tabsetPanel can take an inputId which makes input$inputId reflect the currently selected tab, so your reactive functions could explicitly test if their tabs are visible and return NULL if not.
>
> Okay, I've updated simpleTab to use the id, and I don't think this is the right approach. It may be my slow laptop but I don't think users will be happy staring at a greyed out tab that contains "NULL"  while waiting for the tab to "reactivate":
>
> runGist('4221630')
>
> I understand why it occurs; you've made the tabsetPanel id a reactive input upon which my output functions depend. Therefore they must be updated. However, there's got to be a better way to implement this in the javascript code on the client side.
>
>  One approach is to use "differentiated reactive programming", as defined by the wikipedia article on "reactive programming", and set a higher priority on   propagating data changes to the "visible" tab first, then trickle in the changes from the non-visible tabs.
>
> Or, you could just *not* send data to the non-visible tables until they're visible. This would definitely help the plot issue as well.
>
> I'm going to peek underneath the shiny hood tomorrow and investigate.
>
> >
> > --
> >
> >
>

messages.subject: Re: About multiple reactive plots
messages.body_plain:
What is searchNoun? Is that supposed to be input$searchNoun?

In general, "normal" global variables that are overwritten from reactive functions is a bad "code smell"--i.e., it's not that it's *never* the right answer, but it's almost always a sign that something is wrong. (Global variables that are defined once during startup and just read from reactive functions is fine, though.)

The reason it's a bad code smell is because when you overwrite a normal global variable, reactive functions that read that global variable don't know that anything has changed. The way you generally want to do this instead is to define a reactive function for the variable:

# This appears inside the shinyServer(function(input, output) { ... }) block.
wordcount <- reactive(function() {
  table(input$searchNoun)  # I have no idea what your logic looks like... but make the word count here
})

And then, from both of your reactive plots, call "wordcount()" when you want to access this value. This ensures that when the inputs that affect wordcount change, the reactive plots will know to re-execute themselves.

In case you haven't studied the tutorial chapter on reactivity, here it is:
http://rstudio.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#reactivity

We owe you guys a more in-depth description of reactivity as well, once things slow down a little bit for us (ha!) I look forward to getting that going. Thanks for your patience and please ask more questions if things are unclear.

On Monday, December 10, 2012 1:23:52 AM UTC-8, Yann Richet wrote:
> I am not sure that it is fully related to this discussion thread, but another issue I often experiment is related to multiple input reactives : I want to let the reactive operate, only if two or more input are updated.
> As far as I understand the current model, it is designed to update one output when _any_ of its input are updated.
> For now, we can turn-around that using some "if ((input$...) == no.value) return(NULL)" at the beginning of the reactive function.
>
> I wonder if a signature "update=function(input.new <http://input.new>, input.old)" for the reactive function should allow to include an explicit control over reactive/nonreactive behavior...
> (by default, this function is something like "any(input.new <http://input.new> != input.last)")
> Anyway, I have no idea if it is feasible :) And also it complicates a bit the current model which is fairly simple and efficient...
>
>
> Le samedi 8 décembre 2012 01:47:34 UTC+1, Joe Cheng [RStudio] a écrit :
> > The pain you're experiencing here is the impedance mismatch between the functional-reactive style that Shiny is designed for, and the imperative style ("on click, do this action") that most other GUI frameworks use (certainly most of the ones written before the last 18 months). I believe the functional-reactive style leads to much simpler and concise code, and far fewer errors for 90% of cases, but when you start wanting to do things that are by nature imperative (such as saving to the database) then it starts to get... interesting.
> >
> > I have some ideas about how to allow you to move between one style and the other, but would like to spend a while longer watching what people are trying to do before implementing anything. In this case it seems like your problems could be solved by having a way to access reactive functions/values without actually taking a dependency on them (so that the code doesn't re-execute). Something like:
> >
> > observe(function() {
> >   input$add  # take a dependency on the action button
> >   nonreactive({
> >     # Some logic
> >     saveToDatabase(input$foo, input$bar, input$baz)
> >     # Some more logic
> >   })
> >   # Or another way
> >   saveToDatabase2(nonreactive(input$foo))
> > })
> >
> > So this observer would execute when input$add is clicked, but not when input$foo, $bar, and $baz change. "nonreactive" is a terrible name, but hopefully you get the idea.
> >
> > Any thoughts?
> >
> >
> > On Fri, Dec 7, 2012 at 4:27 PM, Thomas Bristow <darcyspe...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > > I managed to fix my own problem (seems like it), using a global variable as a second counter and some logic. That way the action button will only fire the dependent function once per click - even if other reactive inputs to the function change.
> > >
> > >
> > > UI_____________________
> > >
> > > sidebarPanel(
> > >     selectInput("...", "...",
> > >                 choices = c()),
> > >
> > >     uiOutput("radio"),
> > >
> > >     actionButton("add", "add a mineral")
> > >     ),
> > >
> > > server______________________#partial example
> > >
> > > output$caption <- reactiveText(function(){
> > >   if (input$add==0) {
> > >    count<<- 0
> > > }
> > >   count <<- count
> > >   if (input$add==0 || count == input$add)
> > >     {
> > >     return(NULL)}
> > >    count<<- count+1
> > > return (c(input$min,count))
> > >

> > >
> > >

Exactly, or directly under www and src="autoselect.js" (though aesthetically I think Burkhard's arrangement is better).

It's a common pitfall of HTML in general that you can NEVER do:

<script type="text/javascript" src="autoselect.js"/>

instead you MUST ALWAYS include the closing tag explicitly:

<script type="text/javascript" src="autoselect.js"></script>

See:
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/69913/why-dont-self-closing-script-tags-work
http://tiffanybbrown.com/2011/03/23/html5-does-not-allow-self-closing-tags/

messages.subject: Re: Reactivity and Tabs
messages.body_plain:
It's worth considering attaching a "visibility" or "active" attribute
to each output and only propagating data changes to outputs that are
"visible" or "active". Also, outputs can be declared to override this
attribute if it must be computed on every input change:

   output$plot <- reactivePlot(
      function(){
          cat('output$plot called\n',file=stderr())
          plot(rnorm(input$n))
      },
      overrideVisibility=FALSE
   )

would only invoke the reactivePlot if the output were currently
visible.

An alternative would be to delay the propagation of the input data
changes until an output were visible.

  # Make the plot

If you find yourself with nested reactive functions, that's generally a code smell <http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_smell>. It's great when reactive functions refer to each other:

a <- reactive(function() {...})
b <- reactivePlot(function() { a(); ... })

but not so much when the are actually defined one within the other:

a <- reactive(function() {
  b <- reactivePlot(function() {...})
})

Not saying there is *never* occasion to do that, but I can't think of a scenario where you would.

library(shiny)
library(forecast)

inp <- read.csv("C:/../aggregate-ts-1wt-2wt-mc1v-jul07-nov012.csv")
all1wt <- ts(inp$WT1, freq=12, start=c(2007,7))
all2wt <- ts(inp$WT2, freq=12, start=c(2007,7))
allMc1v <- ts(inp$MC1V, freq=12, start=c(2007,7))
allProd <- ts(inp$AllWTProducts, freq=12, start=c(2007,7))

# Define server logic required to plot various commodities
shinyServer(function(input, output) {

datasetInput <- reactive(function() {
    switch(input$dataset,
           wts1 = all1wt,
           wts2 = all2wt,
           allPs = allProd)
  })
  # display selected commodity names
  output$commSelected <- reactive(function() {
    paste("Commodity selected is:", input$dataset, "for", input$range, "months")
  })

 # Generate a time series table of the requested commodity and only
  # include decomposition chart if requested
  output$CommodityTable <- reactivePrint(function() {
   switch (input$dataset,
wts1 = all1wt,
wts2 = all2wt,
allPs = allProd)
  })

  # Generate a time series forecast plot of the requested commodity and only
  # include decomposition chart if requested
 output$CommodityPlot <- reactivePlot(function() {
 switch (input$dataset,
wts1 = plot(all1wt),
wts2 = plot(all2wt),
allPs = plot(allProd))
 })

})
********************************************************************
ui.R
********************************************************************

library(shiny)

# Define UI
shinyUI(pageWithSidebar(

  # Application title
  headerPanel("Forecasting App"),

  # Sidebar with controls to select the commodity
  sidebarPanel(
    selectInput("dataset", "Commodity:",
                list("1WT" = "wts1",
                     "2WT" = "wts2",
                     "All" = "allPs")),

    sliderInput("range", "Range in months:",
                min=0, max=100, value=24),

    checkboxInput("decompose", "Decompose?", TRUE)
  ),

    # Show the caption and plot of the requested variable
  mainPanel(
    h3(textOutput("commSelected")),
    verbatimTextOutput("CommodityTable"),
    plotOutput("CommodityPlot")
  )
))

messages.subject: Re: reading timeseries datasets into shiny
messages.body_plain:
It's not related to why the plot isn't rendering, but you could replace the switch statement with an environment and get():

dataEnv <- new.env()
dataEnv$all1wt <- ts(...)
dataEnv$all2wt <- ts(...)
# etc.

datasetInput <- reactive(function() {
  get(input$dataset, pos=dataEnv)
})

Everywhere else, just refer to datasetInput()--you don't need to repeat the switch statement (or if you replace it with get(), the get() statement).

This seems like it should work though. The first thing I would do is make a non-Shiny R script to test plotting these different variables and make sure your R code is even correct. Then you can add print() statements (or browser() calls if you're familiar with R debugging tools) to your reactive functions to see when things are executing and what values they're producing.

floader=function(fn){
  temporaryFile <- tempfile()
  download.file(fn,destfile=temporaryFile, method="curl")
  read.csv(temporaryFile)
}

messages.subject: Re: Loading data from https sources
messages.body_plain:
I don't know for sure, but I doubt the RWebsocket issue is related to the https downloading issue. I think your method of downloading files via https should work, especially if it worked in the past.

I recently made a little package called downloader, which tries to abstract away from the details of using internal/curl/wget when downloading https files.
http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/downloader/index.html

You would use it like this:
library(downloader)
download('https://url.com/file.txt")

Depending on the platform and availability of the different download methods (internal/curl/wget/lynx), it'll try different methods of downloading the file.

messages.body_plain:
Is there a way to define a default value for a input that will be generated by a reactiveUI ? My example use-case is the following:

* A select input list is generated based on date
* Other reactive functions utilize inputs like date, result of the select input list, etc to generate further results; these functions validate that the input$date, input$selectListInput are of length > 0 and not empty strings; if they are, they will just ignore the inputs and use the appropriate defaults for them

What happens is that, initially, input$selectListInput is undefined so my reactive functions will process and generate some result while the reactiveUI populates values for them. Once reactiveUI is done, because input$selectListInput now has a different value (went from undefined to the default set in my reactiveUI) and forces the other reactive functions to re-eval again.

The way I got around it for now is that, the main reactive functions don't go any further if the input$selectListInput is length 0 - but this forces me to do additional validation and return a empty data.frame() etc which is visible to the user; however, as soon as the reactiveUI is finished processing, it will then evaluate again with the actual results.

Alternatively, is it possible to define a default value at startup for reactiveUI components - this way, everything else on the page can be rendered and as long as the default value in the reactiveUI is the same as the initial default value, no further re-eval would be needed.

Hopefully the question makes sense

Thanks

-Haider

messages.subject: Re: Plot problem.
messages.body_plain:
Nice!

One piece of advice: if you get rid of the "sglr" directory and move everything in there into the root of the repo, then it's easier for people to install as you can then use Hadley's devtools::install_github <http://www.inside-r.org/packages/cran/devtools/docs/install_github> function.

The boundary plot doesn't show up because of a bug/limitation in Shiny. The client sends the width/height of each plot output, as normal Shiny inputs, so the server can auto-size itself if desired. When a plot is in an element that's hidden, the size is sent as 0/0. Normally, as soon as you change the visibility of the container element, the width/height is recalculated and resent to the server. In this case, you're using a submit button, so that's stopping *all* of the inputs from being sent until submit is clicked--including these width/height values.

One workaround you could use for now is to provide an explicit width/height in your call to reactivePlot, e.g. reactivePlot(function() {...}, width=600, height=400). Either that or get rid of the submit buttons.

One other thing to note. You are using JQuery to show/hide the outputs as the input tabs change. (Was that the only reason you used an index.html file instead of ui.R? Or are you just more comfortable in HTML?) That's OK, but there is also a declarative way to do this in Shiny that you should know about. It is currently broken in your case due to the same problem I described above, but you should know about it anyway:
Give <ul class="nav nav-tabs"> an id attribute, e.g. inputTab
Change <a href="#tab-4469-1" data-toggle="tab" id="powerCalcInp"> to <a href="#tab-4469-1" data-toggle="tab" data-value="powerCalcInp">
Change <div id="powerCalcOut"> to <div id="powerCalcOut" data-display-if="input.inputTab == 'powerCalcInp'">
Repeat for boundary <a> and <div>
Now that's the way it's supposed to work; input$inputTab is now either powerCalcInp or boundaryCalcInp, and you can use data-display-if to control the visibility of arbitrary HTML elements based on that value. But it looks to me like the presence of the submit button breaks it. Since inputTab acts like every other Shiny input, its effect is delayed until submit is clicked, which is not what we want in this case. So if/when we fix the Shiny bug described above then you could move to this model, but probably not before that.

On Thursday, December 13, 2012 10:46:35 AM UTC-8, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> Nice!
>
> One piece of advice: if you get rid of the "sglr" directory and move everything in there into the root of the repo, then it's easier for people to install as you can then use Hadley's devtools::install_github <http://www.inside-r.org/packages/cran/devtools/docs/install_github> function.

Thanks.  Will do.

>
> The boundary plot doesn't show up because of a bug/limitation in Shiny. The client sends the width/height of each plot output, as normal Shiny inputs, so the server can auto-size itself if desired. When a plot is in an element that's hidden, the size is sent as 0/0. Normally, as soon as you change the visibility of the container element, the width/height is recalculated and resent to the server. In this case, you're using a submit button, so that's stopping *all* of the inputs from being sent until submit is clicked--including these width/height values.

That puzzles me because all the outputs below the plot also use the same inputs and they appear to be calculated correctly.  Specifically b0, b1, bp0, bp1, btol of inputs are used for the bottom calculations...

>
> One workaround you could use for now is to provide an explicit width/height in your call to reactivePlot, e.g. reactivePlot(function() {...}, width=600, height=400). Either that or get rid of the submit buttons.
>

Ok, thanks.

> One other thing to note. You are using JQuery to show/hide the outputs as the input tabs change. (Was that the only reason you used an index.html file instead of ui.R? Or are you just more comfortable in HTML?)

Yes, and mathjax (as another requested noted in this forum).

> That's OK, but there is also a declarative way to do this in Shiny that you should know about. It is currently broken in your case due to the same problem I described above, but you should know about it anyway:
> Give <ul class="nav nav-tabs"> an id attribute, e.g. inputTab
> Change <a href="#tab-4469-1" data-toggle="tab" id="powerCalcInp"> to <a href="#tab-4469-1" data-toggle="tab" data-value="powerCalcInp">
> Change <div id="powerCalcOut"> to <div id="powerCalcOut" data-display-if="input.inputTab == 'powerCalcInp'">
> Repeat for boundary <a> and <div>
> Now that's the way it's supposed to work; input$inputTab is now either powerCalcInp or boundaryCalcInp, and you can use data-display-if to control the visibility of arbitrary HTML elements based on that value. But it looks to me like the presence of the submit button breaks it. Since inputTab acts like every other Shiny input, its effect is delayed until submit is clicked, which is not what we want in this case. So if/when we fix the Shiny bug described above then you could move to this model, but probably not before that.

Thanks once again.  Yeah, I need to investigate these capabilities a bit more in the future.

Cheers,

messages.body_plain:
Oh OK. The "RWebSocket unexpectedly closed" in this case is due to an incompatibility between fileInput and glimmer. We're looking into it. fileInput in general is quite flaky right now, if you hadn't noticed. (We're planning on rewriting it completely to be much more robust, but the websockets package we depend on needs to be overhauled first.)

As for the other app you have (that we discussed off-list) that crashes upon starting, the line "starting_value <- input$starting_value" appears outside of any reactive function, which is impossible. If you put input$starting_value directly where you're using it (in the reactive function) then that'd be fine.

If you do want to make a reusable expression based on input values, you need to make a reactive function <http://rstudio.github.com/shiny/tutorial/#reactivity>.

messages.subject: Re: Default value for input generated by reactiveUI
messages.subject_clean: Default value for input generated by reactiveUI
messages.body_plain:
Thank's for the quick reply Joe.

I didn't quite follow your suggestion. I put together a simple app to illustrate what I'm seeing:

ui.R

shinyUI(bootstrapPage(
  textInput(inputId='nords', label='Random Obs: ', value=10),
  uiOutput("selectInputData")
))

server.R

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  genListData <- reactive(function()
  {
    print(paste('Generating List Data - input$nords = ', input$nords))
    c(0, rnorm(input$nords))
  })

  output$selectInputData <- reactiveUI(function()
  {
    print('Output SelectInputData Called...')
    dList = as.list(genListData())

    selectInput(inputId='randomList', label='Random Select List', choices=dList, selected=0)
  })

  output$nullOutput <- reactive(function() {

    print(paste('output$nullOutput func depends on input$randomList - value =', input$randomList))

  })
})

The output generated (no UI interaction) is:

R> shiny::runApp('shinyApp/')

Listening on port 8100
[1] "Output SelectInputData Called..."
[1] "Generating List Data - input$nords =  10"
[1] "output$nullOutput func depends on input$randomList - value = "
[1] "output$nullOutput func depends on input$randomList - value = 0"

So my original issue/question had to do with why output$nullOutput is triggered twice - once when input$randomList is null and then second time it contains the default value that I gave in the reactiveUI function. There is no way in the server.R to set input$randomList = 0 initially (it's valid syntax but the change isn't reflected)

I think reactiveUI, nullOutput, etc in the server.R are evaluated all at the same time - so during the first evaluation round, I don't think it matters if you change the input$randomList value in reactiveUI.

I wonder if there should be a way to initialize reactiveUI components before the server.R evaluates/generates its content - maybe in ui.R

Hopefully the example makes sense

Cheers

-Haider

On Wednesday, December 12, 2012 4:34:42 PM UTC-5, Joe Cheng [RStudio] wrote:
> When the reactiveUI function generates the HTML for selectListInput, you can explicitly tell the selectInput default to be the same as input$selectListInput (although you do have to check for input$selectListInput being NULL). I realize this is a little manual, but I haven't thought of a cleaner way without massively complicating selectInput et al.
>
>
> On Wed, Dec 12, 2012 at 12:14 PM, Haider Ali <haide...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > Is there a way to define a default value for a input that will be generated by a reactiveUI ? My example use-case is the following:
> >
> > * A select input list is generated based on date
> > * Other reactive functions utilize inputs like date, result of the select input list, etc to generate further results; these functions validate that the input$date, input$selectListInput are of length > 0 and not empty strings; if they are, they will just ignore the inputs and use the appropriate defaults for them
> >
> > What happens is that, initially, input$selectListInput is undefined so my reactive functions will process and generate some result while the reactiveUI populates values for them. Once reactiveUI is done, because input$selectListInput now has a different value (went from undefined to the default set in my reactiveUI) and forces the other reactive functions to re-eval again.
> >
> > The way I got around it for now is that, the main reactive functions don't go any further if the input$selectListInput is length 0 - but this forces me to do additional validation and return a empty data.frame() etc which is visible to the user; however, as soon as the reactiveUI is finished processing, it will then evaluate again with the actual results.
> >
> > Alternatively, is it possible to define a default value at startup for reactiveUI components - this way, everything else on the page can be rendered and as long as the default value in the reactiveUI is the same as the initial default value, no further re-eval would be needed.
> >
> > Hopefully the question makes sense
> >
> > Thanks
> >
> > -Haider
> >
> > --
> >
> >
>

server:

messages.subject: Glimmer users: Better error logging now available
messages.subject_clean: Glimmer users: Better error logging now available
messages.body_plain:
Good news for Glimmer users! Up until now, when a hosted Shiny application exits you generally had no way to see what went wrong. We've recently added better error logging that should make it much easier to diagnose such problems.
If the R process is not able to start, an error log is displayed directly in the web browser, if applicable. Example <http://glimmer.rstudio.com/jcheng/badapp/>

Some of you have experienced the "RWebsocket closed unexpectedly" which really means "the app was able to get started but then exited with an error". I changed the wording to be more friendly, and the contents of the log file are now dumped to the JavaScript console. See here <http://webmasters.stackexchange.com/questions/8525/how-to-open-the-javascript-console-in-different-browsers> to learn how to open the JS console in various browsers. You can try it yourself with this example <http://glimmer.rstudio.com/jcheng/terminate/>.

A unique error log file is created in the ~/ShinyApp/log directory each time one of your applications is started by Shiny. You can access this directory using RStudio Server's Files tab or using ssh. These log files are deleted automatically when the process exits, unless the process terminated abnormally (non-zero return code) or at an unexpected time. So if you start to see your ~/ShinyApp/log directory filling up with log files then you know your application is crashing all the time.
Hope that you find this functionality helpful!

messages.subject: reactivePlot that has no output in ui.R causes error : diagnosis and suggested fix supplied.
messages.subject_clean: reactivePlot that has no output in ui.R causes error : diagnosis and suggested fix supplied.
messages.body_plain:
I use reactiveUI to selected between UI types (javascript and rendered).

This means that there can be server reactivePlot elements that are not matched by plotOutputs in the ui. (at any given time).

a simple example:

output$myPlot <- reactivePlot(function() {})

Where

plotOutput("myPlot")

Should NOT exist.

(of course my real plot has actual stuff in, but it doesn't matter, because it's not invoked anyway).

When you execute such a thing on a shiny server it says:

"Error in if (width <= 0 || height <= 0) return(NULL) :
  missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed."

This code matches a snipper in shinywrappers.R.

width and height start out as (default) "auto" but are replaced by

shinyapp$session$get(paste(prefix, name, '_width', sep=''));
etc.

at invocation of the lambda returned by reactivePlot, but before it invokes the actual myPlot function.

I suspect the problem is that shiny is not checking to see if this call to session$get fails (which it must).

Expected behaviour:

no error message

Suggested implementation:

if (is.null(width) || is.null(height) || width <= 0 || height <= 0)
      return(NULL)

Alternative implementation:

Ask session$get to see if the plot itself exists and bail if it doesn't.

Note that this issue also means that a single plot cannot be re-used by multiple output points, which has been noted elsewhere.  I don't know if this is important.

Thanks!

-Alex Brown

1) any time the input xyz is updated AND is different
2) any time the input xyz is updated (different or not)
3) any time any input is updated

xyz <- reactive(function() { input$xyz }

for each input, so as to make xyz a reactive dependency of the output function:

output$myPlot <- reactivePlot(function() {
  plot(xyz())
}

and hopefully is only re-drawn when input is updated and is different than before.

but this seems like wasted boilerplate to me.

-----

output$myPlot <- reactivePlot(function() {
  myxyz = xyz()

  plot(myxyz)

This seems a pain to me; is there a better way?

----

In my side panel I show a multi-list.  If the user selects a single item, then on the right I show a graph and a table.

If the user-selects exactly two, then a second graph is available.  I want to show these as two tabs, one for "this data" and one for "compare these two".

If the user doesn't select a second run, I would like the second tab to be disabled, either not there at all, or greyed out and not clickable.

I have implemented such conditional tabs by using server-side reactiveUI, but I'd prefer to generate them client side using logic like in conditionalPanel.

tabPanel("Ratio", `data-display-if`="input.selection.length == 2",

What do you recommend?  Perhaps tabSetPanel can be changed to have the tab header LI inherit the condition of the child, if there is one?

-Alex

messages.body_plain:
The tab headers are just not designed to be conditional at all, sorry. Certainly they could be, we just didn't design them that way. You could probably do this with a little JS though.

Make the tabsetPanel/tabPanel as normal
Give the tabsetPanel an id attribute (assume "tabs" for this example)
Put a conditionalPanel inside the tabPanel, including an id attribute on the conditionalPanel with a unique value (assume "graph2" for the below example)
Include the following snippet in your ui.R (change tabIndex to be the zero-based tab number, for example tab #2 would be tabIndex=1, tab #3 would be tabIndex=2):
tags$head(tags$script(HTML('
var tabIndex = 1;
$(document).on("shown", "#graph2", function() {
  $("#tabs>li").get(tabIndex).show();
});
$(document).on("hidden", "#graph2", function() {
  $("#tabs>li").get(tabIndex).hide();
});
')))

I haven't actually tried this code but it should instruct the tab button to show when graph2 becomes available and hide when graph2 goes away. If it doesn't work, please send a code sample if possible. Thanks!

> The tab headers are just not designed to be conditional at all, sorry. Certainly they could be, we just didn't design them that way. You could probably do this with a little JS though.

> Put a conditionalPanel inside the tabPanel, including an id attribute on the conditionalPanel with a unique value (assume "graph2" for the below example)

> var tabIndex = 1;
> $(document).on("shown", "#graph2", function() {
>   $("#tabs>li").get(tabIndex).show();
> });
> $(document).on("hidden", "#graph2", function() {
>   $("#tabs>li").get(tabIndex).hide();
> });
> ')))
>
> I haven't actually tried this code but it should instruct the tab button to show when graph2 becomes available and hide when graph2 goes away. If it doesn't work, please send a code sample if possible. Thanks!

>
> On Mon, Dec 17, 2012 at 10:49 AM, Alex Brown <alexb...@gmail.com> wrote:
> > In my side panel I show a multi-list.  If the user selects a single item, then on the right I show a graph and a table.

messages.subject: Developing and testing functions to be used as reactives
messages.subject_clean: Developing and testing functions to be used as reactives
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

  My workflow in R (studio) is to run commands in the console, or write them in the script and use the run command, until it approximates what I need, then make sure the whole script runs the task repeatedly.

  I can't yet see how to easily marry this with the ShinyServer() object and its reactives.

  If I have an existing server, what's the easiest way to test some functions - for example if reactive 'buildData' builds data and I want to prototype a new plot for it? or check the data is still sane?

  Ideally I should have some way to invoke a reactive, either with or without the web client operating, to produce it's data which I can then play with.

  I have some thoughts on how reactive functions might be mutated from their current state, by replacing the non-pure inline calls to reactive dependencies by formal function parameters - which could operate non reactively outside the server, but before I dive into that, I'd love to know how other people approach it.

-Alex

messages.subject: Interactive table example
messages.body_plain:
I've seen a few posts showing nice applications of using shiny with various jQuery table plugins.  I thought I'd share a piece of an app I'm working on that illustrates how easy / possible it is to use shiny to do everything - multi-column sort, pagination, filtering, etc.  This is nice in that all the data operations can be handled in R and just what is being viewed is sent to the browser (I suppose it might be possible to get datatables to do such server-side processing with shiny/R).  There is also some d3 goodness for interactive filtering.

The code is quite messy (and probably buggy) and I probably won't release it until everything is working well and it is all cleaned up.  I hope this will serve as an example of the versatility of shiny.

http://glimmer.rstudio.com/rhafen/awesomeTable/

messages.body_plain:
Probably not efficient, but I normally run a reactivePrint on whatever function I'm testing, then have shiny display the output on a separate tabPanel (I keep one around for scratch work/checking until I'm done). Then I just look at the output to see if it's doing what I want, then tweak it until it does.

messages.body_plain:
Very impressive work, Ryan!

Haider, d3 is pretty low level, much more so than something like googleVis. I do think we will eventually need to establish best practices for how to integrate d3 into Shiny apps, and no doubt Shiny itself will change to make d3 integration easier, but ultimately it's hard for me to imagine a package that would make d3 generally useful for R users (short of an R-to-JavaScript transpiler... *shudder*...)

However, what seems inevitable is that people will build generally useful d3 components and then create R bindings to them. So instead of the "d3 for R" package you might have "plot-d3"[0] or "gis-d3" or "igraph-d3" packages. And of course we would want to ensure that those components can drop right into Shiny.

messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Shiny: v0.2.4
R: v2.15.2
OS: Linux, RHEL4

I'm trying to get shiny up and running on an older RHEL4 server.    I am using the example posted on the homepage (histogram of the faithful dataset), but no png plots are generated. Further, I find the following Javascript errors:

1. WebSocket is undefined in shiny.js, line 417
2. this.$socket.readystate is null or not an object in shiny.js line 527

R is compiled and running well on the machine, and I can export ggplot2 graphics to png -- with a caveat.   I must supply the type=c('cairo') argument to the png function.   My x11 libraries are quite ancient and won't plot with R according to the capabilities() function. However I was able to get pixman and cairo installed correctly (excluding the xrender lib), with built-in support in R (--with-cairo compile time flag).     I can't however get the Cairo package installed, as it complains about some free-type error.     Regardless, I am able to automate png plot export as long as I include the cairo type argument as I mentioned above.

I have modified the server.R code, such that I am passing in the type=c('cairo') argument as follows:

> output$main_plot <- reactivePlot(function() { # function code },type=c('cairo'))
>

Any ideas on what's going wrong, and how this can be fixed?

Thanks in advance

messages.subject: Shiny, D3 and Wide Data (crosspost from d3.js)
messages.subject_clean: Shiny, D3 and Wide Data (crosspost from d3.js)
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

  This is a crosspost from js.d3 that I thought might be of interest here.

  I'm building performance analytic tools for the web at the moment, and am enjoying d3 (http://d3js.org) since I come from R where you are expected to do a similar amount of work for real graphics.

  At the moment I'm using Shiny (http://www.rstudio.com/shiny/) to supply the data, and I have hit a snag.

  Sometimes it's more convenient to supply data to d3 in wide format, either because it's the native format of the data, or it avoid processing on the server side (the client is frankly more powerful).

> Note to the shiny group: My motivation here is that long format is great'n'all in R, but I don't want to transmit it across JSON because my keys are too large.  Really I need to think about relational tables but I have enough on my plate at the moment.  The scheme below is a work in progress, and doesn't include the logic to nest ID keys that I want (think county:state:town), which I've based I pretty hierarchical X axis off.  The answer to all of the below in R, is, of course, melt.  Hooray for R.

  What's wide format?  see end of message for examples, but basically it's like the result of an excel pivot; data is classified some way, such as crimes by type, and the types are arranged as columns.  What's long format? the crime type is a column, and there is a single value column for *crime count*

  I'm struggling to import wide format elegantly into d3 from R.  There are two problems, and the second one is the harder:

First Problem

  Problem 1): R data is formatted as a list (associative map) of typed vectors (arrays).

> USArrests$name=row.names(USArrests)
> str(USArrests)
'data.frame': 50 obs. of  5 variables:
 $ Murder  : num  13.2 10 8.1 8.8 9 7.9 3.3 5.9 15.4 17.4 ...
 $ Assault : int  236 263 294 190 276 204 110 238 335 211 ...
 $ UrbanPop: int  58 48 80 50 91 78 77 72 80 60 ...
 $ Rape    : num  21.2 44.5 31 19.5 40.6 38.7 11.1 15.8 31.9 25.8 ...
 $ name    : chr  "Alabama" "Alaska" "Arizona" "Arkansas" ...

  In Javascript, this becomes:

USArrests={Murder: [13.2, 10, 8.1, 8.8],
 Assault: [236, 263, 294, 190],
 UrbanPop: [58, 48, 80, 50],
 Rape: [21.2, 44.5, 31, 19.5],
 State: ["Alabama", "Alaska", "Arizona", "Arkansas"]}

  But d3 expects an Array of Objects (associative maps).  While this doesn't seem like a hard problem, there's no builtin to d3 to do it, and I've made a mess building one.

  I need to transpose it -  this is conceptually identical to the d3.zip operator, but it takes a map (Object) as input, and an array of objects as output.

  I can muck about with keys as follows - turn it into an un-named list of arrays

USArrests_A=Object.keys(USArrests).map(function(K){return USArrests[K]})

  Transpose it

USArrests_B = d3.transpose(USArrests_A)

Here's what the first sub-array ( USArrests_B[0] ) looks like:

0: 13.2
1: 236
2: 58
3: 21.2
4: "Alabama"

  I need to re-decorate these with names:

 USArrests.C=USArrests.B.map(function(R){
   var A={};
   d3.range(0,R.length).forEach(function(i){
     A[Object.keys(USArrests)[i]]=R[i]});
     return A})

  Here's the first element, USArrests_C[0]:

Assault: 236
Murder: 13.2
Rape: 21.2
State: "Alabama"
UrbanPop: 58

Looks good! - first problem solved, although it was harder than it should be.

So now I have the Second problem

Second Problem

The next problem is that the four crimes - the measured variables (I'm going to assume Urban Pop is a musical crime) are in the same object as the state - the key or experimental variable.

Ideally I want data in the following form:

[ { State: "Alabama", Crime:"Murder", Count:13.2},
  { State: "Alabama", Crime:"Assault", Count:236}, ... ]

Although I would be satisfied with

[ { State: "Alabama", Variable:"Murder", Value:13.2},
  { State: "Alabama", Variable:"Assault", Value:236}, ... ]

This now means that each element of the array corresponds to a single visual element, such as a point, slice of a stacked bar etc.

Side note: A couple of alternative representations are:

> > [ { State: "Alabama", Crimes: {Murder: 13.2, Assault: 236, ... } }, { State: ... }, ... ]
> >
> > and
> >
> > [ { {State: "Alabama"}, {Crime: "Murder"}, 13.2 },
> > { {State: "Alabama"}, {Crime: "Murder"}, 13.2 }, ... ]
> >
> > Which might seem odd, but it allows the keys to be compound or have metadata, which is shared between all crimes in Alabama:
> >
> > [ { {State: "Alabama", Country: "US"}, {Crime: "Murder", Color: "Red"}, 13.2 },
> >
> > However, the first representation is not friendly to d3, and the second is good but outside the scope of my question.

So how do I get here:

[ { State: "Alabama", Variable:"Murder", Value:13.2},
  { State: "Alabama", Variable:"Assault", Value:236}, ... ]

The first problem is that in the original data, the experimental variables (state) are conflated with the response variables, and we need some extra information to extract them.

One approach (taken by R's reshape2 package) is to treat enumerations and strings as experimental and numbers are response variables, which would work in this case, but I'm going to ignore that and just supply the extra missing information.  This seems like an OK strategy to me because I'm going to have to map variables to x and y (and color etc) at some point, and the same basic information is required for that too.

> idKeys = ["State"]
> valueKeys = Object.keys(USArrests).filter(function(x){return x!= idKeys})
["Murder", "Assault", "UrbanPop", "Rape"]

Excellent - but how do I use this information?

Here's where I start to get into trouble, and the fact that I'me been programming javascript for all of 20 hours starts to show.

USArrests_D = USArrests_C.map(function(I){
  return valueKeys.map(function(VK){
    N={};                                         // a new object for each Value Key
    idKeys.forEach(function(IDK){N[IDK]=I[IDK]}); // copy the ID Keys in
    N[VK]=R[VK]; return N;})})                    // and the Value Key

That produces a nested list, which needs flattening:

USArrests_E=[].concat.apply([],USArrests_D)

Which produces the following array:

[{Murder: 13.2, State: "Alabama"},{Assault: 236,State: "Alabama"},... ]

Which is what we want - d3 can nicely process this using the data() function.

The Question:

Is there a better way?  Can d3 add a map zip? What bits of my code could you do shorter, or neater, or with less bugs?  Is this even a problem for anyone else.

I mostly program in R, so please excuse ( but point out ) the inadequacy of my js code.

Appendix: Examples of Wide and Long format:

  Wide format:

> require(reshape2)
> head(n=4,USArrests)
         Murder Assault UrbanPop Rape
Alabama    13.2     236       58 21.2
Alaska     10.0     263       48 44.5
Arizona     8.1     294       80 31.0
Arkansas    8.8     190       50 19.5

Long Format:

> melt(head(n=4,USArrests))
Using  as id variables
   variable value
1    Murder  13.2
2    Murder  10.0
3    Murder   8.1
4    Murder   8.8
5   Assault 236.0
6   Assault 263.0
7   Assault 294.0
8   Assault 190.0
9  UrbanPop  58.0
10 UrbanPop  48.0
11 UrbanPop  80.0
12 UrbanPop  50.0
13     Rape  21.2
14     Rape  44.5
15     Rape  31.0
16     Rape  19.5

messages.subject: Initial thoughts on shiny, ggplot and d3
messages.subject_clean: Initial thoughts on shiny, ggplot and d3
messages.body_plain:
I'm an avid user of Hadley Wickham's http://ggplot2.org, and I want to use the props thus developed to build shiny apps with d3.  This question has come up a couple times on the board, and I want to share my thoughts to spark a discussion of how to make this easy.

I see 4 routes to this being a reality, with different pros and cons.

1) d3 Display backend to R.

Much like R can print to pdf, svg, png, cairo, add a d3 backend.  Interactivity would then have to either be automatic, or retrofitted to metadata in grid, ggplot etc.  This would be solid and widely compatible with R plot types

2) Grid to d3 converter.

Probably easier to write an initial version of, a function which takes a Grid object and sends the primitives to d3.  Likely to be a bulky data format, since the same data may be carried different ways (repeated grob descriptions, implied range in scales and plots etc).  It also would be more difficult to complete since grid is large and extensible.

Would work with lattice and ggplot, but not base plot

3) Ggplot_build to d3 converter

Once you have declaratively specified your plot in ggplot using geoms, scales, data, stats, position, facets and aesthetics, ggplot uses ggplot_build to internally process the data structures - and creates a new object with all of the work done.

This would be a neat place to intercede, although my initial pass over this wasn't as happy as I would like; the data is not truly meant to be human readable, some data is implicit or spread out, and it's possible the format will change in the future.

d3 would need methods for each of the geoms, scales etc, although a small initial working set wouldn't be too hard.  Also allows more flexibility in the form of the output - d3 can do things a bit differently.

Compatible with ggplot but not lattice or base.

4) Complete port of ggplot into d3.

In this scheme, you essentially send the unprocessed ggplot object (or just the declaration) up to d3, and it does all the work.  That's my current approach, since it gets d3 native performance and style, plus lots of flexibility.

Not really compatible with anything except my brain.

---

If I get around to it I'll send some code examples.

-Alex

messages.body_plain:
The way that ggplot2 evaluates arguments in aes() is a little unusual
(it tries to evaluate them in the environment where you called
ggplot()). In your case, it seems that expressions within aes() aren't
able to access the variables in the parent environment, but they are
able to access the columns in the data frame passed to ggplot(). It's
possible that Shiny is not getting the environments quite right. I'll
take a look into that.

To work around this issue, one thing you can do for the vlines is to
take the xintercept out of aes(). So instead of this:
  geom_vline(aes(xintercept=e), color="red", linetype="dashed")
You have this:
  geom_vline(xintercept=e, color="red", linetype="dashed")

As for the layers where you have the aesthetic mapping depend on the value of x:
  layer(data = d, mapping = aes(x=ifelse(x > e,x,e), y=y), geom = "area",
    geom_params=list(fill="#00A5FF",alpha=.3))

This is a bit unusual - if I understand it correctly, you want to
compare the values in the column d$x to the single number stored in
the variable e; for each row, use the larger of the two values. You
could work around this by creating a new column in d, called xe, with
something like this:
  d$xe <- ifelse(x > e, x, e)

Then use aes(x = xe, y=y).

-Winston
