messages.body_plain:
I'm not 100% sure this is what you're looking for, but you can use
split() to turn it into a list of data frames, where there is one list
element for each row of the original data frame. Each of these list
elements is a one-row data frame with the same original columns.

For example:
> x <- split(USArrests, seq_len(nrow(USArrests)))
> head(x, 3)
$`1`

        Murder Assault UrbanPop Rape
Alabama   13.2     236       58 21.2

$`2`
       Murder Assault UrbanPop Rape
Alaska     10     263       48 44.5

$`3`
        Murder Assault UrbanPop Rape
Arizona    8.1     294       80   31

> str(x)
List of 50
 $ 1 :'data.frame': 1 obs. of  4 variables:
  ..$ Murder  : num 13.2
  ..$ Assault : int 236
  ..$ UrbanPop: int 58
  ..$ Rape    : num 21.2
 $ 2 :'data.frame': 1 obs. of  4 variables:
  ..$ Murder  : num 10
  ..$ Assault : int 263
  ..$ UrbanPop: int 48
  ..$ Rape    : num 44.5
 $ 3 :'data.frame': 1 obs. of  4 variables:
  ..$ Murder  : num 8.1
  ..$ Assault : int 294
  ..$ UrbanPop: int 80
  ..$ Rape    : num 31

The elements are named "1", "2", and so on, but you can remove the
names with unname(x).

-Winston

messages.body_plain:
I think I've figured it out. The issue is with ggplot, not shiny. If
you take a look at ggplot.data.frame, you'll see that it defaults to
use the global environment for evaluating the aes() stuff:

> ggplot2:::ggplot.data.frame
function (data, mapping = aes(), ..., environment = globalenv())
 ...

The solution is to specify ggplot(environment=environment()), so that
it evaluates the stuff from aes() inside of the calling environment,
instead of inside the global environment.

So instead of this:
  plot.2 <- ggplot(data = d, mapping = aes(x = x, y = y)) +
You would have this:
  plot.2 <- ggplot(data = d, mapping = aes(x = x, y = y), environment
= environment())

I've put the code at:
  https://gist.github.com/4349072

I'll have to talk to Hadley about whether the global environment thing
is a bug or feature in ggplot2.

-Winston

messages.body_plain:
Yes, glimmer.rstudio.com <http://glimmer.rstudio.com> uses Shiny Server which will be available in late January as a beta (more details <http://blog.rstudio.org/2012/12/04/shiny-update/>). Shiny Server uses the SockJS library for NodeJS <https://github.com/sockjs/sockjs-node> to simulate websockets over regular HTTP, so it works fine with MSIE8/9.

This technique isn't possible using the Shiny R package alone because there is no SockJS library available for R.

Thanks and sorry for the inconvenience.

messages.subject: Pressing Enter after entering text when using invalidateLater()
messages.subject_clean: Pressing Enter after entering text when using invalidateLater()
messages.body_plain:
I have an app at http://glimmer.rstudio.com/gsee/BATS/

It shows market data for a user-specified stock.  It uses invalidateLater() so that the prices update every second (although to the user it will appear to update every 5 seconds because that is how often the data provider updates their data)

If the user types GOOG, it will update and start showing data for Google.  However, if the user types GOOG and then hits Enter, it will reset the app and data for SPY will be shown.  I tried adding an Update button, and that works, but then the prices only update when the user clicks the button.

Any suggestions for a way for the user to be able to hit enter after typing a new ticker symbol (which seems to be what most people do naturally)?

[A version of the code that is very similar to] code for that app is available at https://gist.github.com/4340065.  To actually run the code, you'd need the latest version of quantmod and qmao which are only available  on R-Forge. quantmod: https://r-forge.r-project.org/scm/?group_id=125 and qmao (which is currently only available by checking out via svn) https://r-forge.r-project.org/scm/?group_id=1113

Thanks,
Garrett

>   ..$ UrbanPop: int 58

> > progress, and doesn't include the logic to nest ID keys that I want (think

> >
> >
> >   What's wide format?  see end of message for examples, but basically it's
> > like the result of an excel pivot; data is classified some way, such as
> > crimes by type, and the types are arranged as columns.  What's long format?

> >   I'm struggling to import wide format elegantly into d3 from R.  There are

> >
> > First Problem
> >
> >   Problem 1): R data is formatted as a list (associative map) of typed
> > vectors (arrays).

> >> str(USArrests)
> > 'data.frame': 50 obs. of  5 variables:

> >  State: ["Alabama", "Alaska", "Arizona", "Arkansas"]}
> >
> >   But d3 expects an Array of Objects (associative maps).  While this doesn't
> > seem like a hard problem, there's no builtin to d3 to do it, and I've made a
> > mess building one.
> >
> >   I need to transpose it -  this is conceptually identical to the d3.zip
> > operator, but it takes a map (Object) as input, and an array of objects as
> > output.
> >
> >   I can muck about with keys as follows - turn it into an un-named list of
> > arrays
> >
> > USArrests_A=Object.keys(USArrests).map(function(K){return USArrests[K]})
> >
> >   Transpose it
> >
> > USArrests_B = d3.transpose(USArrests_A)
> >
> > Here's what the first sub-array ( USArrests_B[0] ) looks like:
> >
> > 0: 13.2
> > 1: 236
> > 2: 58
> > 3: 21.2
> > 4: "Alabama"
> >
> >   I need to re-decorate these with names:
> >
> >  USArrests.C=USArrests.B.map(function(R){
> >    var A={};
> >    d3.range(0,R.length).forEach(function(i){
> >      A[Object.keys(USArrests)[i]]=R[i]});
> >      return A})
> >
> >   Here's the first element, USArrests_C[0]:
> >
> > Assault: 236
> > Murder: 13.2
> > Rape: 21.2
> > State: "Alabama"
> > UrbanPop: 58
> >
> > Looks good! - first problem solved, although it was harder than it should
> > be.
> >
> > So now I have the Second problem
> >
> > Second Problem
> >
> > The next problem is that the four crimes - the measured variables (I'm going
> > to assume Urban Pop is a musical crime) are in the same object as the state
> > - the key or experimental variable.
> >
> > Ideally I want data in the following form:
> >
> > [ { State: "Alabama", Crime:"Murder", Count:13.2},
> >   { State: "Alabama", Crime:"Assault", Count:236}, ... ]
> >
> > Although I would be satisfied with

> > [ { State: "Alabama", Variable:"Murder", Value:13.2},

> >

> > },
> >
> >

> >
> >

messages.subject: Noisy reactives keep shouting
messages.body_plain:
I know this has been mentioned a few times, but now it's starting to cause me pain.

Reactives that aren't in the current tab *please* shouldn't fire.  I generally keep drill down views in the back tabs, and since these require 2 orders of magnitude more data to be sent up, I don't want them firing while the user is exploring the front tab.

I had set it up so that reactives with the following roles were wired together:

1) input de-noisers: for instance I want to know if there are 1 input variables or 2.  instead of consuming the input variables I have a reactive which eats both and says 1 or 2
2) database fetchers
3) middleware to clean up the database results
4) graph drawers / data uploaders

I have now started to move the two middle layers to plain old functions, to reduce the chatter that seems to happen even if I don't care about a result right now.

I'm happy to say this seems to work, and reactive inputs consumed by plain functions that are themselves consumed by reactive outputs seems to have the right effect.

But I'm say to see all those funky brackets going.

Note: my app is split into 4 views

1) d3 javascript overview graph (200 json objects with 4 fields)
2) d3 javascript detail graph (2000 json objects with 20 fields)

3) ggplot png version of 1
4) ggplot png version of 2

each of the above also has a co-output which throws a plain data table up beneath the graph.

This means that when all reactives are firing, I'm moving 2 pngs, 2x2000 rows of tables, 2x200 rows of tables, and data for two jsons.

Realistically the user is looking at 2 at once, and would like to press next rapidly to move between records.

BTW: does shiny zlib compress on the wire?

-Alex

Thanks for the lovely tool, btw, I'm going to be using this for lots of stuff.

messages.subject: Re: Noisy reactives keep shouting
messages.body_plain:
Thanks for the feedback, Alex!

Winston, Jeff and I have been talking about this kind of stuff recently; we are considering changes to the reactive system to allow entire parts of the reactive graph to be turned off automatically as you tab around. It's pretty tricky to get right (i.e. maintaining correct results!) so it's hard to predict if/when these changes will land in Shiny. However I believe there is some low hanging fruit that will at least make the situation a good deal better.

In the meantime the best workaround I can offer (which you are probably doing) is to give the tabsetPanel an ID, and make sure your output reactives do a check to see if the corresponding tab is active and immediately return NULL if not. You could do this in reactive functions as well if you want, it would help but possibly not as much as you think it would. I would expect a single extra execution for any reactive that is only depended on by outputs that are not visible AND check for whether their tabs are selected at the beginning of their reactive output function. I am hoping to explain why in a blog post over Christmas break (though it is a complicated topic and I am a VERY slow writer, so no promises...).

Shiny isn't currently able to compress on the wire. (Note that it's websocket compression we're talking about, not HTTP, so it's not very widely supported yet on the server side.)

messages.subject: Enable and disable UI elements in the "input" and "output" R objects
messages.subject_clean: Enable and disable UI elements in the "input" and "output" R objects
messages.body_plain:
>From previous discussions, it seems that the easiest way of having having a dynamically defined number of inputs or outputs is done by choosing a reasonable maximum number of possible number of inputs/outputs and defining a numbered set inputs/outputs up to the maximum number, e.g.

MAX <- 200

lapply(seq_len(MAX), function(i) {
   output[['impl']]$defineOutput(
      paste("dynamicOutput_", i, sep=""),
      reactive(function() {
         paste("Dynamic input ", i, " will go here but it depends on input dummy=", input$dummy, sep="")
      })
   )
})

Then, based on some user input, the actual number of these elements that are used could be much smaller than MAX.  An example could be that I want a user input for each column of a data frame, where I don't know the number of columns of the data frame up front, and the number of columns will change throughout the application.

Now suppose I want MAX to allow for the possibility of many inputs/outputs (hundreds), but the actual number will typically be quite small (< 10).  This number will be changed relatively infrequently in the application.

Further suppose that these dynamic UI elements also depend on some other input, which changes frequently.

Setting MAX to anything too large will cause updating to be very slow, even if only a few of the elements are actually being used.

I have a simple gist that illustrates this.  There is a numericInput that lets you choose the number of dynamic elements to show, and a dummy input on which all of these elements depend.  Setting MAX to be too large really bogs things down.

runGist("4383290")

What would be nice would be to have the ability such that when the definition of the number of dynamic elements to show is changed, to be able to disable elements in the "input" or "output" shiny R objects that will not be used.

Maybe there is an easier way around this?

messages.subject: Re: a data analysis GUI using shiny?
messages.subject_clean: a data analysis GUI using shiny?
messages.body_plain:
I put a partially-working hack of a data-analysis menu using shiny on github (https://github.com/mostly-harmless/damshiny.git)

As you will see there is not that much there just yet. I see it as a 'proof-of-concept' of what I am trying for. I also posted the files as a Gist. The following should work, if not please let me know.

library(shiny)
shiny::runGist('4385800')

I have a number of questions and would love to hear suggestions on how to do this better. If you would like to contribute directly, even better.

1. I used fileInput to allow a user to load data. I couldn't determine how to get ui.R and server.R to use the file however.
2. I'd also like a list of data.frames available for analysis. The 'is.data.frame' code on lines 4 and 5 seems to work outside of the app but not inside.
3. How to create a vector of variable names from the selected dataset that can be used in model specification?
3. Is using 'conditionalPanel' the way go here? Is there a way to avoid putting the if(input$tool == '') arguments in each reactive function separately? I got an error when I tried to put the if-statement around a set of reactives.
4. What about an html form with GET (e.g., localhost:8100?tool=reg)? How would you setup the if-statements to get the desired inputs and outputs to show?
5. For the comparison of means the Correlation tab could be dropped. I saw some discussion about this but it wasn't clear to me how to implement the suggestions.
6. Plots don't show completely (have to scroll). Is there a way to make the output window longer?
7. For larger datasets I might want to turn-off reactive features. Is that possible and if so how?

messages.subject: Data Analysis Menu using Shiny - Version 0.01
messages.subject_clean: Data Analysis Menu using Shiny - Version 0.01
messages.body_plain:
I put a pre-alpha data-analysis menu on github (https://github.com/mostly-harmless/damshiny.git). I also posted it as a Gist. The following should work, if not please let me know.

library(shiny)
shiny::runGist('4385800')

I have a number of questions and would love to hear suggestions for improvement. If you would like to contribute directly, even better.

1. Main question: Does the structure I used in server.R make sense? Is it (reasonably) efficients? If not how could efficiency be enhanced? Note that I plan to add 10-15 more 'tools' to the menu once the basic code-structure is a bit more solid.
2. Errors are printed when data or variables have not yet been selected. Is there a clean way to avoid this across various functions?
2. I saw some discussion about conditional tabs but it wasn't clear to me how to implement this. Suggestions?
3. How to provide a list of data.frames in memory available for analysis? I tried sapply(mget(ls(),.GlobalEnv),is.data.frame) but couldn't get it to work inside the shiny app.
4. Plots don't show completely (have to scroll). Is there a way to make the output window longer?
5. Is it possible to make the window for a selectInput with multiple=TRUE longer (e.g., height based on the number of variables in a data.frame)?
6. If a variable has been selected as a dependent variable could that easily be removed from the list of independent variables?
7. Can dropdowns in shiny have sub-menu's (e.g. regression could have, say, two sub-options: linear and logistic). I could put-in a conditional selectInput I guess.
8. For larger datasets I might want to turn-off reactive features. Is that possible and if so how?

messages.subject: question related to input of data using shiny
messages.subject_clean: question related to input of data using shiny
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am interested in seeing if I can use Shiny to input data into a database. I have created a tiny app to check how I might do this (here I am not yet using a database). The app is in

http://glimmer.rstudio.com/rdabbler/testForm

and the code is in gist:

https://gist.github.com/4410797

In this app, once I select "projects" in dropdown, I have an option of selecting "view projects" or "add projects". When I select  "add projects", the mainpanel shows a text box to add projects to an existing dataframe. To avoid changes as I am typing in the text box, I also have a drop down with choices ("Choose","Update") so that the reactive function runs only when the choice is set to "Update". That works fine. However after that, if I forget to set back the option to "Choose", then if I start typing something in the text box, it starts adding those to the data (which I don't want). Is there a way to automatically reset the option in the drop down to "Choose" in server.R after running the reactive function to add data.

The one option I was thinking of is using submit button but that is not convenient for the case where I want to generate reactiveUI (one drop down is generated based on choice of another dropdown).

Also, if there are other ways of implementing inputs of form data, I would be interested in those too.

Thanks,
Shankar

messages.subject: uploading files to locally running app
messages.subject_clean: uploading files to locally running app
messages.body_plain:
In case it might be useful for others ... It took me some time to get this working but the following works in my app.

When the app starts and when the upload box gets checked (or unchecked) the user is asked to select a file. I understand an action button will be added to the main shiny package at some point, until then this works ok.

In ui.R

    checkboxInput("upload", "Load data by (un)checking the box", value = FALSE),

In server.R

  output$dataloaded <- reactiveUI(function() {

    # adding 'input$loaded' makes sure this function gets called when input$upload changes (on-to-off or off-to-on)
    input$upload
    filename <- file.choose()
    newdata <- load(filename, envir = .GlobalEnv)
    data_sets <<- unique(c(newdata,data_sets))

    selectInput(inputId = "dataset", label = "Data sets", choices = data_sets, selected = data_sets[1], multiple = FALSE)
  })

messages.subject_clean: uploading files to locally running app
messages.body_plain:
Yann Richet suggested using fileInput. It got it to work. Code below.

For an example see:

shiny::runGist('4385800')

server.R

loaddata <- function(state) {
  inFile <- state$upload
  if (is.null(inFile))
    return(NULL)

  filename <- inFile$name
  ext <- file_ext(filename)
  file <- newdata <- sub(paste(".",ext,sep = ""),"",filename)
  ext <- tolower(ext)
  if(ext == 'rda' || ext == 'rdata') {
    newdata <- load(inFile$datapath, envir = .GlobalEnv)
  }
  # by putting this here we get the name of the object inside the R data file
  data_sets <<- unique(c(newdata,data_sets))

  if(ext == 'sav') {
    assign(file, read.spss(inFile$datapath), envir = .GlobalEnv)
  } else if(ext == 'dta') {
    assign(file, read.dta(inFile$datapath), envir = .GlobalEnv)
  } else if(ext == 'csv') {
    assign(file, read.csv(inFile$datapath, header = TRUE), envir = .GlobalEnv)
  }
}

  output$dataloaded <- reactiveUI(function() {
    # adding 'input$loaded' means the function gets called when input$upload changes
    # by putting it in this function the list of data also gets updated
    input$upload
    loaddata(as.list(input))

    # Drop-down selection of data set

    selectInput(inputId = "dataset", label = "Data sets", choices = data_sets, selected = data_sets[1], multiple = FALSE)
  })

ui.R

     fileInput("upload", "Load data (Rdata, CSV, Spss, or Stata format)")
